browse: Unified Browserbase CLI for browser automation, cloud APIs and the local Functions dev server

checks.why: functions dev server, CLI commands and driver discovery
CLI lint rules incl. config rules

risks.text: `browse functions dev` puts a random 32-byte token into the runtime API path and 404s runtime poll/response/error requests without it; changing the route or the worker URL without the token lets any local caller on the port read invocations or post results.

bin/run.js loads .env from the cwd with dotenv, which never overrides variables already set in the shell, so a stale shell export silently beats the .env value; BROWSE_LOAD_DOTENV=0 turns loading off and the default is slated to flip.

The Node version gate in bin/run.js reads engines.node from package.json (>=22.18.0, same as the SDK); change the engines range and the runtime check and error message follow it, so keep it aligned with the SDK and CONTRIBUTING.

Local Chrome discovery trusts a DevToolsActivePort file only after the port's live /json/version reports the same websocket path, because another process often rebinds 9222; skipping that probe attaches to the wrong browser.

groups.title: The in-browser Stagehand runtime (Chrome extension) serving act/extract/observe over CDP JSON-RPC, with the understudy page/frame/context layer

checks.why: extension runtime through a fresh build
extension types

risks.text: Domain policy changes are serialized on context.domainPolicyTail and the new policy is published only after Chrome's DNR rules were installed; the runtime also resets the policy to null when the Stagehand instance is disposed, so skipping the queue or the reset leaks a policy into the next session.

ensureBrowserConnection rebuilds the browser session whenever the CDP URL differs from the stored one; keep browserSessionCdpUrl set and cleared with the session, or re-initialization keeps talking to the old browser.

Cross-origin iframes (OOPIFs) are adopted as child CDP sessions with ownership seeded for their subtree, including ones that existed before attach and nested ones; changes to page.ts or frame.ts that skip adoption or pass no progress tracker break act/locators inside iframes and ignore screenshot/pdf/waitForSelector deadlines.

act() substitutes %name% variables into action arguments, but not into drag-and-drop arguments, which are selectors that page-controlled names must not rewrite; cached-action replay substitutes again.
The extension bundle is generated by vite build and embedded in each SDK; its tests run `pnpm run build` first, so edit sources and rebuild instead of patching bundles.

groups.title: Adapters that expose Stagehand to agent hosts (Cursor, fx, Codex, Claude, Mastra, Vercel AI, Deepagents, Eve, pi) and their SDK session wrappers

checks.why: fx session environment and layout
Deepagents adapter and eval runner

risks.text: Agent hosts see exactly three Stagehand tools (run, snapshot, screenshot); there is no navigate or start tool, so docs and prompts must open URLs with `run` and page.goto, and for fx must use the exact mcp_stagehand_* names, never invented ones.
fx harness sessions must set FX_SOUND=off (with FX_SKIP_ONBOARDING, FX_AUTO_UPGRADE=0, FX_NO_OPEN_BROWSER) so a non-interactive run does not play sounds or prompt.
claude-cua-sdk makes one paid Anthropic messages.create call per turn in a loop bounded only by input.maxTurns; keep that limit set.

groups.title: The JSON-RPC protocol: Zod schemas, generated stagehand.v4.json and versioning; the contract for the extension and every SDK

checks.why: regenerates stagehand.v4.json from schemas.ts

risks.text: stagehand.v4.json is generated from schemas.ts by `pnpm --filter ./packages/protocol build` and the Python and Go models are generated from it; edit the schema, then run `just generate` and commit the regenerated files or `just check` fails on drift.
Model IDs are validated only as non-empty strings without whitespace so new provider models work without a release; do not turn them back into closed enums.
Telemetry export is opt-in: the telemetry config needs an explicit traces endpoint ending in /v1/traces and nothing is sent by default; do not add a default endpoint.
The protocol version drives compatibility: a new capability a client may require is a minor, a breaking wire change is a major; the changeset type must match.

groups.title: Python SDK (`stagehand` on PyPI): launches Chrome with the extension and drives the runtime; models generated from the protocol

checks.why: the Python SDK tests
generated models match the protocol schema

risks.text: Everything under src/stagehand/_generated/ is output of scripts/generate.py from stagehand.v4.json; hand edits are overwritten and fail the --check drift test.
browser.py launches Chrome with a fixed flag list including WebMCP features and --remote-allow-origins=*; a missing or renamed flag silently disables WebMCP or blocks the extension's CDP connection.

The extension is discovered automatically; the extension_id parameter is deprecated and ignored, and extension_cdp_url must be the browser-level websocket the extension dials from inside the browser, not necessarily the client's own.
The SDK targets Pydantic v2 (pydantic>=2.12,<3) and builds requests with model_validate; v1 calls such as .dict() or parse_obj will not work.

groups.title: Root config, docs and build tooling for the pnpm and uv workspaces

checks.why: formatting, lint, types, release metadata and Python generated-code drift
vitest, pytest and Python cookbook checkpoint tests

risks.text: `pnpm install` covers only the TypeScript workspace; the Python projects share the root uv.lock and .venv and need `just install` (uv sync --locked); after a dependency change run `uv lock` from the root and commit it with the member pyproject.toml.
`just` recipes prefixed with _ are internal release commands (_version, _publish-*); running them directly versions or publishes packages.
`just generate` rebuilds the protocol, Python models and extension bundle; run it after touching packages/protocol and commit the output.

The nested Deepagents runner and examples must be run with `--project` (repo root) and `--package`, because their intermediate pyproject.toml stops uv's workspace discovery; use the just recipes (check-deepagents, test-deepagents) instead of bare uv commands.

rules.rule: Change protocol schemas first, then the extension and every client; regenerate with `just generate` and commit the generated files.
rules.why: The Python and Go models and stagehand.v4.json derive from the protocol; stale output fails `just check` and breaks clients at runtime.

checks.why: formatting, lint, types, release metadata and generated-model drift

rules.why: The next generate run overwrites it and the drift check fails.

rules.rule: Run `just changeset` for changes to a public SDK, the extension or the protocol contract, selecting only the packages to release.
rules.why: Without it nothing ships, since releases are driven by the Changesets release PR.

rules.rule: An extension fix is released by also selecting each SDK that should ship it.
rules.why: The extension is embedded in each SDK and not published separately, so users never get the fix otherwise.

rules.rule: Compatible correction is a protocol patch, a capability new clients may require is minor, a breaking wire change is major with a coordinated release.
rules.why: The runtime protocol version is the compatibility check between SDK and extension.

rules.rule: Target each stacked PR at its immediate predecessor; after a squash merge S, merge S^ and then `-s ours` S into the child and confirm the child's files are unchanged with git diff.
rules.why: Otherwise the child PR diff shows or reverts the parent's changes.

rules.rule: Cursor and fx integrations expose only the run, snapshot and screenshot tools; use exact names (mcp_stagehand_*) in fx and never invent navigate/start tools or launch a separate browser.
rules.why: Invented tool names fail in the host and a second browser bypasses the persistent Stagehand session.

rules.rule: browse functions dev runtime endpoints must require the per-run random token.
rules.why: Otherwise any local process on the port can poll invocations or post results.

rules.rule: Domain policy is applied through the serialized queue and cleared when the Stagehand instance is disposed.
rules.why: A leaked or racing policy blocks navigation in the next session.

rules.why: Users' traces would otherwise be sent off-machine without consent.
